entries.title: Clip sharing: recipient galleries, suggested posts that carry the share link, and clips with no event
entries.summary: Share clips with speakers, sponsors, exhibitors, attendees and your team from **Share all** and **Share selected** on the Clips page. Each person gets a private gallery with their clips, grouped by **All together**, **Session** or **Date shared**, with **Download all** and posting to LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Email and LINE. The suggested post ends with the person's share link, and **Post to LinkedIn** publishes the text as shown. Clips cut from a recording with no event now ask which event the people belong to. **Media → History → Clip sharing** shows what each person did.

where.path: Marketing → Media → Clips → Share all

entries.use_case: Organizers get speakers, sponsors and teammates to post their own clips, with a link back to the event on every post, and see who opened and shared what.

cs_action.note: Default on for organizations with Clips; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how speakers or sponsors can post session clips, or wants to know who shared them.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Clips with speakers, sponsors or exhibitors.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Clips → Share all
internal.gotchas: Voices must be named in Speakers to tag before clips reach a speaker. Needs the matching web-api release.
internal.talk_track: Pick the clips, pick the people, and each one gets a page of their own moments with a post already written.

entries.title: Clip pages: a public page for every shared clip, with your button, links, search setting and per-clip numbers
entries.summary: Every shared clip has a public page with the player, the speakers and the transcript, in the event's brand. Set the button, up to six links, whether visitors can download and whether search engines can find the pages in **Media → History → Clip sharing → Clip page settings**, for one event or for every event. A clip's **Sharing** panel shows views, shares by channel, links copied, downloads, button clicks and visits from shared links, and a switch keeps one clip out of search. **Clip sharing** results add **Page views**, **Page shares** and **Button clicks**.

where.path: Marketing → Media → History → Clip sharing → Clip page settings

entries.use_case: Organizers turn a shared clip into a page that sends viewers to the event website and can be found in search, and see which clips did the work.

cs_action.note: Default on for organizations with Clips; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer wants shared clips to drive registrations or site visits, or asks whether clip links can be found in Google.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer sharing clips from an event with a website.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → History → Clip sharing → Clip page settings
internal.gotchas: Search is on by default for clip pages. Turn it off per event before sharing if speakers have not agreed to publish.
internal.talk_track: Each shared clip now has a page of its own with your button on it, and you can see which clips sent people to your site.

entries.title: Copy a public link to a clip from its menu, its page or a selection
entries.summary: **Copy public link** is now in a clip card's **⋯** menu and in the clip page's **More actions**, and **Copy public links** is in the selection bar's **More actions** for several clips at once. The link belongs to the event, not to a person, and its views, shares, downloads and button clicks count as **Direct link** in the clip's **Sharing** panel. A hidden clip, a clip still rendering and a clip with no event say why no link is offered.

where.path: Marketing → Media → Clips → ⋯ → Copy public link

entries.use_case: Organizers can post a clip from their own account or paste it into a newsletter without sharing it with anyone first.

cs_action.note: Default on for organizations with Clips; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer wants one link to a clip to post themselves.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Clips.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Clips → ⋯ → Copy public link
internal.gotchas: Needs the web-api release before the web-ui-v2 release.
internal.talk_track: Every clip now has a link you can copy and post yourself, and we count the visits as Direct link.

entries.title: Edit a registration form question's label, options and required setting
entries.summary: Organizers can now edit an existing registration form question — changing its **Label**, **Options** and **Required** toggle — without rebuilding the form. Existing answers are preserved when options are renamed or removed. Changes are tracked in event history and can be restored.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Registration

where.path: Marketing → Registration → Form → Questions

entries.use_case: When a registration question needs a wording correction or a new answer option added after the form is live, organizers can edit it in place rather than deleting and recreating it — keeping all previously collected answers intact.

cs_action.note: Available within the Registration beta; no separate enablement needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to fix a typo in a live registration question or add a missing answer option without losing existing responses.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Registration beta who needs to update form questions post-launch.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Registration → Form → Questions
internal.gotchas: Organization-level questions are overridden per-event (Module_Field_Overrides) rather than changed globally; standard questions only accept the Required toggle. Dropped options are removed from the list but stored answers are untouched.
internal.talk_track: You can now edit registration questions live — fix labels, add options, or flip required — and every answer already collected stays safe. The change is logged so you can restore the previous state if needed.

draft.docs_gap: The /registration/forms guide should document how to edit an existing question (label, options, required), note that org-level questions are overridden per-event, and explain that removing an option does not delete collected answers.
draft.why_use_it: The registration form question editor lets you refine questions after your form goes live. Update a label for clarity, add or remove answer options, or toggle a question between optional and required — all without losing any answers registrants have already submitted. Changes are logged in event history so you can review or roll back any edit.

entries.title: LinkedIn connect completes reliably and shows why it failed
entries.summary: Connecting a LinkedIn account from the clip share page, clip preview, speaker verification, Creator share card, Dispatch kit, Creator video panel, campaign gallery, and the **Promote** page now completes correctly even when LinkedIn's sign-in window cuts off communication with the opener. Every failure — cancelled, closed, expired, refused, or blocked — shows a specific toast message. After a successful connect the button updates to **Post to LinkedIn** without a page reload.

where.path: Marketing → Clips → Share  /  Marketing → Campaigns → Share kit  /  Speaker portal → Share your event card

entries.use_case: Speakers and team members who click "Connect LinkedIn" on a clip or share card now see the connection complete and the button change to "Post to LinkedIn" — or get a clear message if something went wrong — so they are never left wondering whether the connect worked.

cs_action.note: Fix shipped by default; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer or speaker reports that clicking 'Connect LinkedIn' did nothing, left the button unchanged, or gave no error message.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Clips, Dispatch share kits, Advocacy share cards, or the speaker portal share card where LinkedIn connect is available.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Clips → Share  /  Speaker portal → Share your event card → Connect LinkedIn
internal.gotchas: Both the web-UI PR (#1717) and the companion web-api PR (same branch name) must be deployed together for the fix to work end-to-end. The PR notes no human has clicked through a real LinkedIn sign-in with this build yet.
internal.talk_track: LinkedIn's own sign-in pages block the pop-up from talking back to the page that opened it. The fix adds a dedicated return page that hands the result back over a broadcast channel, so the connect always finishes and any failure shows a plain-language reason.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section explaining the LinkedIn connect flow on the share card — what the pop-up does, what each failure toast means, and how to retry.

entries.title: Bring your speakers, sponsors or VIPs when signing up for Advocacy
entries.summary: During the Marketing sign-up flow for Advocacy, a new **Who should be sharing it?** step lets you paste a list of names and emails or upload a CSV before your account is created. The preview cards update to show the people you brought, and after sign-up the rows that have an email are automatically added to **People**. A summary card reports how many were added, already existed, or were not added.

where.path: Marketing sign-up → /signup?focus=advocacy → Who should be sharing it?

entries.use_case: An organizer signing up for Advocacy can paste their speaker roster or sponsor list right in the sign-up flow, so their advocates land in People the moment the account is created — no separate import step needed.

cs_action.note: Default-on step in the Advocacy sign-up conversation; no flag to flip.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a prospect or new customer asks how quickly they can get their speakers or sponsors into Advocacy after signing up.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer starting a new Sessionboard Marketing account via the Advocacy sign-up path (/signup?focus=advocacy).
internal.staff_path: /signup?focus=advocacy — the 'Who should be sharing it?' step appears between the event step and the email step.
internal.gotchas: Only the Advocacy door (/signup?focus=advocacy) shows this step; webinars, field events and other doors are unchanged. Maximum 200 people and 24,000 characters of field data per import; the sign-up copy tells the user to import the rest later in People. Rows without an email appear in the preview count but are not imported. The role column (Speaker, Gold Sponsor, etc.) is shown on the share card preview but is not written to People because the import API has no role field.
internal.talk_track: When you sign up for Advocacy you can paste your speaker list or drop in a CSV right in the conversation — your people are in the system before you even reach the dashboard.

draft.docs_gap: The get-started guide should document the 'Who should be sharing it?' step in the sign-up conversation, including the paste/CSV options, the 200-person cap, what gets imported to People, and what the post-sign-up summary card shows.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing's sign-up conversation walks you through creating an Advocacy campaign before you ever reach the dashboard. Bringing your people list at sign-up means your speakers, sponsors or VIPs are already in People and ready to invite the moment your account is live. You can paste names and emails, drop in a CSV with up to 200 rows, or skip and explore with sample data — whichever fits where you are in your planning.

entries.title: Sign-up flows open on the question that matches what you brought
entries.summary: Adding **`?bring=`** to a sign-up link tells the sign-up conversation what the person arrived with — a speaker/sponsor list, caption word list, last year's award categories, or a question bank — and opens on the question that collects it. The opening line names what they brought, and the question order adjusts so the most relevant step comes first.

where.path: Sign-up pages: /signup/marketing, /signup/awards, /signup/learning

entries.use_case: When a site page or ad links someone who already has a speaker list, caption glossary, award categories, or question bank, append the matching `?bring=` value so the sign-up conversation greets them with the right question immediately — reducing drop-off from a generic opening.

cs_action.note: URL parameter; no toggle needed. Works automatically when the link includes the parameter.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants to link to a sign-up from a landing page or ad where the visitor already has a specific asset (speaker list, award categories, question bank, caption words).
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running targeted acquisition campaigns for Marketing (beta), Awards, or Learning sign-ups.
internal.staff_path: Append ?bring=list, ?bring=glossary, ?bring=categories, or ?bring=questions to the relevant /signup/* URL.
internal.gotchas: Only the four documented values work per sign-up; unknown values and cross-product values are silently ignored. Marketing's list and glossary questions still appear after the event name is collected — only the opening wording changes for those. Not tested in a browser per the PR.
internal.talk_track: If you're driving sign-ups from a page where visitors already have their speaker roster or last year's award categories, add ?bring=list or ?bring=categories to the sign-up link so the first question they see is the one that takes what they brought.

draft.docs_gap: The get-started guides for Marketing, Awards, and Learning should document the supported ?bring= values, their effects on question order and opening wording, and example links for each sign-up.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing, Awards, and Learning each start with a short sign-up conversation that collects the details needed to set up your program. When you link someone from a page or campaign where they already have something specific in hand — a list of speakers, a set of award categories, or a question bank — the `?bring=` parameter lets the conversation open on the question that takes it, with wording that names what they brought. The rest of the setup continues in the usual order.

entries.title: Clips posted to LinkedIn now include the clip's share link
entries.summary: When a clip is posted natively to LinkedIn from the clip share page, the person's tracked share link is automatically appended on its own line at the end of the post text. If the link is already present in the caption, it is not added a second time. Long captions are trimmed with an ellipsis to stay within LinkedIn's 3,000-character limit, and the link is always preserved.

where.path: Marketing → Clips → Share → Post to LinkedIn

entries.use_case: Speakers and advocates who post a clip natively to LinkedIn no longer need to manually paste their share link — viewers can tap through directly to the clip page, driving traffic back to the event's content.

cs_action.note: Bug fix shipped automatically; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that LinkedIn clip posts had no link back to the clip page, or that viewers couldn't find the original content.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Clips with LinkedIn sharing enabled.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Clips → Share → Post to LinkedIn
internal.gotchas: Only native LinkedIn video posts are affected; Media campaign posts (publishLinkMediaToLinkedIn) are unchanged.
internal.talk_track: Clips posted to LinkedIn now automatically end with the speaker's personal tracked link, so every viewer can reach the clip page and organizers can attribute the traffic.

draft.docs_gap: The Clips guide should note that LinkedIn posts automatically include the share link at the end of the caption, and explain the 3,000-character trimming behaviour.
draft.why_use_it: Clips let speakers and advocates share short video highlights from sessions directly to social media. Because LinkedIn native video posts carry no link card, appending the share link gives every viewer a direct path back to the full clip page. Each person's link is tracked, so organizers can see exactly who drove views and clicks.

entries.title: Trial workspaces can send a small first batch of reviewer and sharing invitations without a card
entries.summary: Self-serve workspaces in trial with no card on file may now send a limited first batch of real invitations: up to **5 awards reviewer invitations** and up to **25 speaker-sharing invitations** (Advocacy campaigns). The batch is counted once per workspace, never replenished, and the workspace owner receives one email when it is used up. Any send that would exceed what remains is refused with a clear message showing how many are left and how many were requested — no partial sends occur.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable SELF_SERVE_FREE_BATCH; then the limit applies automatically when inviting reviewers or launching a speakers_share Advocacy campaign

where.path: Awards → Programs → Reviewers (reviewer invitations); Marketing → Campaigns → Launch (sharing invitations)

entries.use_case: Lets a trial customer invite a handful of real reviewers or share their event with a small group of speakers before committing a card, so they can validate the workflow end-to-end during the trial period.

cs_action.note: Feature is off by default behind the SELF_SERVE_FREE_BATCH flag. Must be enabled by support or engineering before any trial workspace can use it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a trial customer on Awards or Marketing asks why they cannot send reviewer invitations or launch a sharing campaign without a card.
internal.who_should_get_it: Self-serve trial workspaces that have not yet added a card and want to test reviewer invitations (up to 5) or speaker-sharing Advocacy campaigns (up to 25).
internal.staff_path: Awards → Programs → Reviewers; Marketing → Campaigns → Launch
internal.gotchas: The batch is counted once per workspace and never refilled — even if invitees are removed. A failed send still consumes the batch. Re-inviting the same person counts again. Sends larger than the remaining quota are refused entirely (no partial send). The reviewer file-import path is also blocked if the file exceeds the remaining quota. Only verified-email users can trigger the batch. The batch only applies while the product trial is active.
internal.talk_track: During your trial you can invite up to 5 reviewers and share with up to 25 speakers without a card, so you can see the full workflow before committing. Once the batch is used, adding a card unlocks unlimited sends — nothing is charged during the trial itself.

draft.docs_gap: The awards trial and self-serve billing guides should document the free-batch limits (5 reviewer invitations, 25 sharing invitations), the all-or-nothing refusal behaviour, the owner notification email, and the fact that the count is permanent and per workspace.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Awards lets you run a complete awards program — from collecting nominations to scoring and announcing winners — without leaving your event platform. Inviting reviewers and sharing the program with speakers are the first real actions that prove the workflow works for your team. The free batch lets you complete those steps during a trial so you can evaluate the full experience before adding a payment method.

entries.title: Get started: Live captions and transcripts card added to Marketing
entries.summary: A **Live captions and transcripts** card now appears in the **Get started** Marketing group. Selecting it takes you directly to **Events → Live captions** for your organization, where live captioning is available on every Marketing plan at no extra charge.

where.path: Get started → Marketing → Live captions and transcripts

entries.use_case: Helps organizers on any Marketing plan discover and navigate to live captioning without hunting through the sidebar — useful when onboarding a new team member or setting up a first event.

cs_action.note: Default-on discovery card; no enablement required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Marketing customer asks how to find or start using live captions, or during onboarding walkthroughs of the Get started page.
internal.who_should_get_it: All Marketing plan customers — caption hours are included on every Marketing plan.
internal.staff_path: Get started → Marketing → Live captions and transcripts
internal.gotchas: The card links to Events → Live captions at the org level; the actual captioning tool lives per-event. The card has no capability toggle — live captions are always available.
internal.talk_track: Live captions are already included in your Marketing plan. The new Get started card takes you straight to the tool so you can set it up before your next event.

draft.docs_gap: The get-started guide should mention the Live captions and transcripts card and link to the Live Transcribe guide.
draft.why_use_it: Live captions and transcripts let you capture spoken session content as text in real time, making your event more accessible and giving you a ready-made transcript to repurpose into clips, recaps and other content. Every Marketing workspace includes caption hours, so there is nothing extra to purchase. Reach for it whenever you want to serve attendees who are deaf or hard of hearing, or when you want a searchable record of what was said on stage.

entries.title: Clip tiles show a neutral placeholder while their thumbnail loads
entries.summary: On the public clips share page, the **Speaker Portal**, and the Creator console, each clip tile now shows a neutral grey surface while its thumbnail loads, then fades the image in smoothly. A thumbnail that fails to load leaves the neutral tile instead of showing a broken image, and there is no layout shift during loading.

where.path: Marketing → Clips (share page, Speaker Portal, Creator console)

entries.use_case: Clips shared publicly or with speakers no longer show a black box for several seconds while thumbnails load — the gallery looks polished from the first paint, which matters when speakers or attendees are viewing shared clip pages.

cs_action.note: Visual fix; no action needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer or speaker reports that the clips gallery shows black boxes or broken images before thumbnails appear.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Clips (limited release) whose speakers or audiences view the public share page.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Clips → share page (/clips/:token)
internal.gotchas: The black background is intentionally preserved behind a successfully loaded thumbnail so letterboxed clips still look correct.
internal.talk_track: The clips gallery now loads cleanly — tiles show a neutral grey placeholder and fade in the thumbnail once it arrives, so the page never looks broken.

draft.docs_gap: The Clips guide should note that clip tiles display a neutral loading state while thumbnails fetch, and that failed thumbnails fall back gracefully without a broken-image icon.

entries.title: Clip gallery tiles load instantly instead of showing a black screen
entries.summary: Thumbnail images on the clip gallery (public share page, Speaker Portal, and Creator console) now load from the content CDN at the correct tile size. Previously, tiles stayed black for roughly 8 seconds because each request generated a new presigned S3 URL that the browser could not cache.

where.path: Marketing → Clips

entries.use_case: Anyone viewing a clip gallery — whether on the public share link, in the Speaker Portal, or in the Creator console — now sees thumbnail images appear immediately instead of waiting several seconds for a black tile to resolve.

cs_action.note: Fix is default-on. A kill switch (CLIP_GALLERY_CDN_THUMBNAILS=false) exists if issues arise, but no customer action is needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that clip gallery tiles appear black or take a long time to load.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Clips.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Clips
internal.gotchas: The kill switch CLIP_GALLERY_CDN_THUMBNAILS=false reverts tiles to the old presigned S3 URL without a code deploy. The share email (clip-share.js) is unaffected by this change.
internal.talk_track: Clip gallery thumbnails now load from the CDN edge at the right tile size, so they appear instantly and are cached by the browser.

draft.docs_gap: The Clips guide should note that gallery tile thumbnails are served from the content CDN and are browser-cacheable.

entries.title: Opening an event now lands on Home instead of the Dashboard
entries.summary: Links that open an event — including the event switcher in the sidebar, the org events page, upcoming event cards, the redirect after creating an event, and **View Event** on the global home — now navigate to the event's **Home** page instead of the **Dashboard**.

where.path: Sidebar event switcher; Org Events page; Global Home → View Event

entries.use_case: Organizers land directly on the Ask-powered Home page when they open any event, so they immediately see what needs their attention rather than having to navigate away from the Dashboard.

cs_action.note: Default behaviour change; nothing to enable. The Dashboard is still reachable from the sidebar.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why clicking an event no longer opens the Dashboard, or reports that the landing page changed.
internal.who_should_get_it: All organizers on standard events; lite, webinar and field events are unaffected.
internal.gotchas: Reviewers who are not on the Event Team, and anyone on an org where PLATFORM_ASK_HOME_FOR_EVERYONE is off, still land on the Dashboard. The Dashboard row in the sidebar and direct /dashboard URLs are unchanged. The simplified shell (org events page) still opens events at /overview.
internal.talk_track: When you click into an event, you now land on Home — the Ask-powered page that shows what needs your attention — instead of the Dashboard. The Dashboard is still one click away in the sidebar.

draft.docs_gap: The "Home or Dashboard" section of the Organization Home guide should note that all standard event entry-point links (event switcher, org events page, View Event, post-creation redirect) now open the event at Home, and list the exceptions (reviewers not on the Event Team, the simplified shell, and direct /dashboard links).
draft.why_use_it: Organization Home surfaces the tasks, submissions, and records that need your attention across all your events in one place. Use it as your daily starting point to find what is waiting for you, ask questions about your program, and jump straight into the work — without hunting through individual event dashboards.

entries.title: Platform Home: stat tiles link to tools, guided first-run screens, unified Ask, and a "From Sessionboard" media row
entries.summary: The event and org **Home** pages gain four improvements: stat tiles are now clickable links to their respective tools and are hidden when no data is available; tool cards show **See what it does** (a preview dialog) and **Set it up**; empty **Surveys**, **Submissions**, and **Agenda** tools open a guided first-run screen with starter templates and an Ask prompt; Ask is unified so **Home**, the top bar, and the Dashboard all open the same conversation — **Expand** opens it full-screen, **Dock** returns it to the side panel; and a **From Sessionboard** row surfaces recent webinars and blog posts from the Sessionboard community feed.

where.path: Home

entries.use_case: Organizers landing on Home can jump directly to the tool they need by clicking a stat tile, get a guided starting point when a tool is empty, and ask questions in a single consistent Ask conversation no matter where they open it — reducing the time it takes to go from landing on Home to doing real work.

cs_action.note: Shipped as a default-on improvement to Home for all customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When onboarding new customers, demoing the platform, or when a customer asks how to get started with an empty tool like Surveys or Agenda.
internal.who_should_get_it: All platform customers — especially new ones who benefit from the guided first-run screens and the unified Ask experience.
internal.staff_path: Home (event or org level)
internal.gotchas: The 'From Sessionboard' media row only appears when the community feed at /community/media is reachable and returns items; an unreachable feed silently hides the row rather than showing an error. The old Agent window (/ai/* routes) is removed; any bookmarked links redirect into Ask on Home.
internal.talk_track: Home now does more of the orientation work for you — stat tiles take you straight to the right tool, empty tools walk you through setup, and Ask is always the same conversation no matter where you open it.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new stat-tile links, the tool-card preview dialog and Set it up action, the guided first-run screens for Surveys/Submissions/Agenda, the unified Ask surface (Expand/Dock/panel), and the From Sessionboard media row.
draft.why_use_it: Home is the starting point for every event and organization in Sessionboard. It surfaces the numbers that matter, points you to the tools that need attention, and keeps Ask — the AI assistant — one click away whether you are working in a side panel or full-screen. Use it to orient yourself at the start of a work session, hand off context to a colleague, or let a new team member find their footing without a guided tour.

entries.title: One custom domain now serves every public page of your organization
entries.summary: A single custom domain can now be designated to serve all of an organization's public pages — agent Sites (`/p/<slug>`), event pages (`/e/<slug>`), Sites (`/s/<slug>`), and the org home page — so every link the platform generates uses that domain. Organizers can also set or change the **Home page** for a domain via **Marketing → Pages → Domains → [domain] → Home**.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Site Domains; then Marketing → Pages → Domains → [domain] → Home

where.path: Marketing → Pages → Domains

entries.use_case: Organizers who want every public link — event pages, speaker Sites, agent pages, and the org home — to appear under a single branded domain rather than a mix of Sessionboard subdomains and per-page custom domains.

cs_action.note: The serves_org_pages flag is set per org via a support or CSM request; no self-serve toggle exists yet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why their event-page or Site links still show sessionboard.io instead of their own domain, or when they want a single vanity domain for all public pages.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with an existing custom domain add-on who want unified branding across all public-facing pages.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Pages → Domains → [domain] → Home
internal.gotchas: Only one domain per org can have serves_org_pages set. The Worker routing companion (cloudflare-workers#57) and public-api routes (sessionboard-public-api#276) must also be deployed for end-to-end routing to work.
internal.talk_track: With this on, every link Sessionboard generates — event pages, speaker portals, Sites, agent pages — uses your domain automatically. You set the home page once and the rest is handled.

draft.docs_gap: The /settings/domains guide should add a section explaining how to designate one domain as the org-wide domain that serves all public pages, and how to set or change the home page for that domain.
draft.why_use_it: Site Domains let you replace Sessionboard's default public URLs with your own branded domain across every surface your audience sees. When one domain is designated as the org-wide domain, all links the platform builds — for event pages, speaker Sites, agent pages, and the organization home — automatically use that domain, keeping your brand consistent without manual link management.

entries.title: Event Home cards and tool rows respect each team member's permissions
entries.summary: On the event **Home** page, cards, in-use rows, stat tiles, the **All tools** section, and the preview dialog now check what the signed-in user may do. When a permission is missing, **Open** and **Set it up** buttons are disabled with the standard permissions tooltip instead of leading to a page that refuses access. In-use rows and stat tiles lose their links; the row stays focusable with `aria-disabled` and the tooltip on focus. **Turn on preview** and **Request beta** in the Early Access section are also disabled for users without **Manage Early Access**. **See what it does** always remains available.

where.path: Event → Home

entries.use_case: Teams that give reviewers, coordinators, or vendors limited event roles no longer see those users land on access-denied pages after clicking a working button on the Home page — the button is disabled with a clear explanation before they ever click.

cs_action.note: Default on; no action needed. Restricted users will now see disabled buttons instead of broken links.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that limited-role users (reviewers, coordinators, vendors) were hitting access-denied pages after clicking Home page buttons.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with team members on restricted event roles.
internal.staff_path: Event → Home
internal.gotchas: A small set of tools (Poster Gallery, Contracts, Title Slides, Advocacy, Event Website, Transcriptions, Ready Room, Attendee Mobile App, Clips, Event Recaps, Content Galleries, Credit Claiming, Registration, Expo Sales) have no event-level permission guard today, so their actions remain enabled for all roles.
internal.talk_track: If someone on your team has a limited role, the Home page now shows them exactly what they can and cannot open — disabled buttons with a tooltip — instead of letting them click through to a page that turns them away.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document that Home cards, in-use rows, stat tiles, and the Early Access actions are permission-aware, and list which tools check which permissions before enabling Open or Set it up.

entries.title: Clip sharing: clearer counts, distinct Share buttons, conditional gallery heading, and accessible logo plate
entries.summary: The **Share** wizard header now reads "**X clips ready to share**" instead of "All X clips in this event", so the count matches what the wizard actually shares. The Clips page now shows two distinct buttons: **Share all** in the header and **Share selected** in the selection bar. A contact's private gallery shows "**Moments from your sessions**" only when they appear in at least one clip; otherwise the page reads "**Clips shared with you from [event]**". When a Brand Kit band colour is set, the logo plate gains a 2 px ring in the band's ink colour to keep the plate boundary at WCAG 1.4.11 contrast.

where.path: Marketing → Media → Clips → Share all / Share selected

entries.use_case: Organizers get accurate clip counts in the Share wizard so they know exactly how many clips are going out, and recipients see a heading that reflects whether they actually appear in any clips.

cs_action.note: All fixes are default-on for organisations with Clips; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer notices the clip count in the wizard differs from the Clips page, or asks why a recipient sees a generic heading instead of 'Moments from your sessions'.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Clips with the clip sharing feature.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Clips → Share all
internal.gotchas: The wizard count and the Clips page count intentionally differ: the page counts every size and unfinished clips; the wizard counts only clips ready to share.
internal.talk_track: The wizard now tells you exactly how many clips are going out, and each recipient's page reflects whether they're actually in any of those clips.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the wizard count ("clips ready to share") differs from the Clips page count, which includes all sizes and unfinished clips, and that the recipient gallery heading changes based on whether the contact appears in at least one clip.

entries.title: Review guest seat requests in a side drawer from the Guests tab
entries.summary: Opening a guest registration from the **Guests** tab — or clicking **View request** on any row, or following the **View request** link in a Slack seat-request post — slides open a **Request** drawer showing every form answer, the registrant's organization and type, other requests from the same organization (click to switch), and who approved or declined the request and when. The **Approve**, **Waitlist**, and **Decline** buttons in the drawer call the same route as the table, and the decision rewrites the original Slack post.

where.path: Marketing → Events → [event] → Guests → View request

entries.use_case: When a seat-request notification arrives in Slack, the team can click View request to open the full registration details and approve, waitlist, or decline without switching to a different page — and the Slack post updates automatically to reflect the decision.

cs_action.note: Default on for events using Field Events and the Guests tab; no enablement step required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer uses Slack for seat-request approvals and wants their team to review full registration details without opening a separate admin page.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running in-person field events with seat-request workflows and Slack connected.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Events → [field event] → Guests → View request
internal.gotchas: Requires the matching web-api release (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5588). The drawer deep-link uses the URL param ?tab=guests&registration=<id>, so direct links from Slack will only work once both releases are live.
internal.talk_track: Your team gets a Slack ping when someone requests a seat. They click View request, see the full form answers and every other request from that organization, and approve or decline right there — the Slack post updates itself.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the Request drawer: how to open it via the View request button or the Slack deep link, what information it shows (form answers, organization, related requests, decision audit line), and how Approve / Waitlist / Decline from the drawer updates the Slack post.
draft.why_use_it: Running an in-person field event means fielding seat requests from many organizations at once. The Guests tab gives you a single place to see every registration, review the answers each person submitted, compare requests from the same organization side by side, and record your decision — all without leaving the page. Connecting Slack means your team can act on requests the moment they arrive, and the Slack post always reflects the latest status.

entries.title: Coordinator agent: out-of-office, bounce and list mail no longer trigger AI replies or count in metrics
entries.summary: The **Coordinator** agent now classifies every inbound email as human, auto-reply, bounce or list mail before acting on it. Out-of-office messages, delivery failures and mailing-list replies are stored as read and marked, but the AI reply run is skipped and those messages are excluded from conversation counts, unread counts, the 7-day response rate, average response time and send-volume reply totals. Bounce messages record the bad address on the inbound row so it is visible in the run. Human replies — including messages whose subject merely mentions "out of office" — continue to queue the AI run and count in all metrics as before.

where.path: Agents → Coordinator → Run history / Conversations

entries.use_case: Organizers using the Coordinator to chase speaker tasks no longer see vacation auto-replies inflate unread counts or response-rate metrics, and the AI does not waste a reply run drafting a response to an out-of-office message.

cs_action.note: Behaviour change is automatic; no flag to flip. Existing jobs queued before this release fall back to the old isAutoReply check, so a brief transition period is expected.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer complains that their Coordinator response rate looks wrong, or that the AI drafted a reply to a vacation message.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer actively using the Coordinator agent to chase speaker tasks.
internal.staff_path: Agents → Coordinator → Run history
internal.gotchas: Jobs already in the queue before this deploy use the old four-header isAutoReply check. The new ?filtered= query param on the conversations list is backend-only in this release — no UI toggle yet, but the data is there for a future filtered view.
internal.talk_track: The Coordinator now tells the difference between a real reply and an out-of-office, so your response rate and unread count only reflect speakers who actually wrote back.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that auto-replies, bounces and list mail are filtered from conversations and metrics, and that a bounce records the bad address on the inbound row in run history.
draft.why_use_it: The Coordinator agent sends follow-up emails to speakers on your behalf and tracks their replies so you always know who has responded and who still needs a nudge. It filters out automated noise — out-of-office messages, delivery failures and mailing-list traffic — so the conversations list, response rate and unread count reflect only genuine human replies. When a message bounces, the Coordinator records the bad address so you can act on it without digging through raw email logs.

entries.title: Advocacy companion pages and share composer respect Arabic and other RTL languages
entries.summary: The Advocacy companion page and **Promote** page now open in the campaign's language (or the language the visitor picked), including Arabic and other right-to-left languages, without showing English first. Share text boxes in the **Still**, **Video** and **Media** composers follow the direction of the text, so Arabic reads right to left and English left to right. The campaign builder's **Live** simulation previews the campaign language instead of the admin's. After a reload, saved Arabic text comes back as saved, and switching the share text back to the campaign's language restores the campaign's text.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaign → Live simulation; the advocate's companion and Promote pages

entries.use_case: Organizers running Arabic-language events can now send advocates to the companion page and share composer without those pages flashing English or rendering RTL text incorrectly. Advocates writing their own Arabic post copy see it flow right-to-left as expected.

cs_action.note: Default-on fix; no action needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer running an Arabic-language event reports that the companion page shows English briefly or that share text appears in the wrong direction.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Advocacy with a non-English or RTL campaign language, especially Arabic.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaign → Live simulation
internal.gotchas: Radix popovers inside the Live simulation still render in the admin's locale — this is a known limitation noted in the PR.
internal.talk_track: Arabic-speaking advocates now see the page in Arabic from the moment it loads, and their post copy flows right-to-left automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the companion page honours the visitor's language preference (via ?lng= or stored pick) and that share text boxes automatically switch text direction to match the script being typed.
draft.why_use_it: The Advocacy companion page and share composer let speakers, sponsors and attendees personalise and post their own event card to LinkedIn, X, WhatsApp and other channels. When your event is in Arabic or another right-to-left language, the page loads in that language from the first paint and share text boxes automatically switch direction to match the script the advocate types in.

entries.title: Advocacy: suggested post drafts now match the link's language and include event dates
entries.summary: The suggested post drafts in **Make it yours** are now written in the share link's language (the campaign's, else the event's, else the organization's) instead of English, and drafts saved earlier in another language are not shown. They now name the event's own dates, not the day the campaign was created. Switching the share text to another language without editing it no longer keeps the old language's text.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → [Campaign] → Make it yours

entries.use_case: Organizers running multilingual Advocacy campaigns — for example Arabic-language events — can now trust that every advocate sees draft posts in the correct language with accurate event dates, without needing to manually correct the copy.

cs_action.note: Automatic fix; no enablement needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that Arabic (or any non-English) advocates see English draft posts, or that the AI-generated post mentions the wrong date.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Advocacy with non-English share links or multilingual campaigns.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → [Campaign] → share link → Make it yours
internal.gotchas: Changing only the language (no new text) clears the saved text written in the previous language, so the advocate sees the campaign's text in the new language. Text the advocate edited and saved in the same language is kept. An Arabic-language campaign can't be translated into English from the picker yet; the page keeps Arabic and says so.
internal.talk_track: Advocates now get draft posts in their own language with the right event dates — no manual cleanup needed after launch.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that draft language follows the share link's content_language (campaign → event → org fallback) and that event dates are included in the AI prompt so generated posts reference the correct dates.

entries.title: Embeds show each speaker's job title and company for that session
entries.summary: When a speaker has a job title and company set for one session (**Job title & company for this session** on the session's **Participants** tab), the **Speaker List** and **Speaker Gallery** embeds now show it inside that session, and the schedule embed's search finds the session by it. Sessions without their own value show the contact's job title and company as before, and the speaker card itself keeps the contact's values.

where.path: Program → Embeds → Speaker List / Speaker Gallery

entries.use_case: Organizers who assign different job titles or companies to a speaker per session (e.g. a speaker who presents as CEO for one session and as a Board Member for another) will now see those distinctions correctly reflected inside the speaker list and gallery embeds on their website.

cs_action.note: Bug fix; no action needed. Customers using Role Attributes with speaker or speaker-gallery embeds will see the correct per-session affiliations automatically.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that their speaker gallery or speaker list embed shows the wrong job title or company when a speaker appears in multiple sessions with different roles.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Role Attributes (on_request) with speaker list or speaker gallery embeds.
internal.staff_path: Program → Embeds → Speaker List or Speaker Gallery
internal.gotchas: Only public seats are included; per-session values only appear inside the session detail view within the embed, not on the top-level speaker card, which continues to show the contact-level default.
internal.talk_track: If a speaker presents as CEO for one session and Founder for another, the embed now shows the right title in each session — the speaker card still shows their default.

draft.docs_gap: The embeds guide should note that per-session job title and company values (Role Attributes) are respected inside session speaker cards in the Speaker List and Speaker Gallery embed types.

entries.title: A copy of your Onboarding Sandbox is a real event
entries.summary: Cloning an Onboarding Sandbox used to copy its sandbox label too, so the new live event showed the sandbox banner. The copy is now a normal event with no sandbox banner.

where.path: Events → event menu → Clone

entries.use_case: Customers who build their live event by cloning the Onboarding Sandbox get a normal event without the sandbox banner.

cs_action.note: For events cloned before this fix: Event → Settings → Admin Settings → Onboarding sandbox event off. To unlock deleting events after kickoff: Organization Settings → Admin Settings → Onboarding mode off (staff only).

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer's live event still shows the sandbox banner, or they can't delete events after onboarding.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every newly onboarded customer.
internal.staff_path: Organization Settings → Admin Settings → Onboarding mode; Event Settings → Admin Settings → Onboarding sandbox event
internal.gotchas: Both switches are staff only and save as soon as you flip them.
internal.talk_track: Your live event is a real event from the moment it's copied; we switch onboarding mode off after your kickoff so you can tidy up sample events.

entries.title: Animated cinematic card works in every share language
entries.summary: The cinematic Animated card failed to build for share languages it had no words for, such as Japanese. Those languages now get the English words on the card, and the rest of the share stays in the chosen language.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaign → Animated card

entries.use_case: Advocacy campaigns in any of the 29 share languages can use the cinematic Animated card.

cs_action.note: Default-on fix.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports the Animated card not rendering for a non-English campaign.
internal.who_should_get_it: Advocacy customers with non-English campaigns.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaign → Animated card
internal.gotchas: Only English, German, Spanish, French and Arabic have their own cinematic words so far.
internal.talk_track: The cinematic card now works whatever language the campaign is in.
